name: 01_service_arcade
title: A / SERVICE ARCADE
detail:
Primary proposal: organize ALL FOUR services along the WEST SIDE WALL in ONE continuous reclaimed-steel arcade, 24 metres long with four generous recessed bays under one warm-lit canopy. It is a functional station concourse with coherent architecture, not a row of freestanding screen vending machines. The main title 'PLAYER HUB' spans the arcade; small paired category plaques 'APPEARANCE' and 'CAREER' make two adjacent groups. In order along the frontage: 'LOCKER', 'PRIZE COUNTER', 'PROFILE', 'PROGRESSION'. All four labels and distinct bays should be identifiable in the wide view.
Locker: the hero bay with three full-height dented personal lockers, an angled dressing light, a small coat/hat rail and a simple outfit stand matching the character scale. A small vertical mirror is dark or simply reflective; no cloned crowd. Prize Counter: adjacent set-back staffed-looking-but-unoccupied repurposed ticket window, low brass-edged counter and one small outfit/helmet cabinet; quiet secondary signage. Profile: compact angled identity terminal plus one portrait plaque and a few restrained pennants. Progression: a long physical transit-route-like milestone display on the wall with three lit nodes and a small trophy shelf, giving it a horizontal silhouette instead of a second upright screen.
At each bay create a shallow marked approach apron separated from the through-route by floor material, not tall barriers. Leave a generous 6-metre circulation lane in front. Brick/tile pilasters separate bays so the architecture organizes the kiosks. A blue cat with black fedora stands on the open apron. The round pit edge is visible in the right foreground, open and uncluttered; the north event board beyond it stays clearly visible. Warm practical ceiling fittings and subtle graffiti only at the edges. Make the main shot an eye-height three-quarter view along the full arcade, not frontal flat UI.
Bottom detail vignettes: left show the paired Locker + Prize Counter architecture with caption 'APPEARANCE'; right show Profile + the long milestone wall, caption 'CAREER'. Main title exact 'A / SERVICE ARCADE'.
prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept / architectural game-environment design.
Asset type: a polished landscape concept board for the user's Godot game One Gun, a third-person arena shooter with stylized cat characters and a secret underground event culture.
Image inputs: image 1 is the actual existing F6 scene, including the exact blue-and-cream cat character with black fedora; use as the spatial and character reference. Image 2 is the original subway concept art, reference ONLY for worn tile, reclaimed steel, warm practical lights, discreet vibrant signage and inhabited atmosphere; do not copy its crowded layout, eight-player pads or invented menu features.
Keep the recognizable tall vaulted subway shell and shallow round social pit of the existing scene, real gameplay proportions, clear wide circulation and visible event destination. Develop the kiosk architecture to look professionally authored, cohesive and achievable in a modest-budget stylized 3D game. Camera at normal third-person player height, with the existing cat in the foreground as a scale reference; never an isometric diorama or miniature model. Do not turn the cats into humans or redesign their bodies. Modest props density, believable construction, warm neutral materials with restrained color. No holographic tables, floating UI screens, dense bloom, volumetric fog, nightclub lasers, combat, extra guns or NPC shopkeepers.
Visual hierarchy: main EVENT BOARD uses acid yellow; PLAYER HUB has a single muted magenta address; social cyan; practice orange; green reserved for actual ready state. Within the hub use white service lettering, distinct physical props and small icons, not four equally loud colored billboards. Strong silhouettes, comfortable spaces for third-person camera, flat accessible kiosk approaches and a clear continuous route around the pit. Prize browsing is optional and away from the mandatory event route.
Output: one large landscape design board, about 3:2 aspect ratio. Upper 76% a beautiful wide player-perspective environment concept. Lower 24% a clean dark design strip with two small detailed vignettes and very short readable captions that explain the kiosks, not a paragraph of tiny text. The image should be attractive enough to present to the game's creator while honestly depicting an architectural proposal. Label the top left with the specified concept title, and bottom right small 'CONCEPT STUDY'. No gameplay HUD, no unrelated logos, no current player's account name or balances. Render all specified main labels accurately.

name: 02_two_clubrooms
title: B / TWO CLUBROOMS
detail:
Primary proposal: keep the central pit and main concourse very open, but move four kiosks into TWO OPEN CLUBROOM ALCOVES off the WEST side. These are adjacent rooms with distinct large portals, NOT one straight four-counter arcade and NOT an island. A shared overhead directional sign 'PLAYER HUB' identifies this side of the station. The near/south portal is 'APPEARANCE': inside, 'LOCKER' on the near interior wall with coat rails, lit outfit stand and dented lockers; 'PRIZE COUNTER' in the deeper side corner, an optional second stop. The far/north portal is 'CAREER': 'PROFILE' is an identity desk on one wall and 'PROGRESSION' is a long milestone/trophy wall opposite, with a small worn bench in a recess. Each room has a 7-metre-wide open mouth, level access, no doors and enough depth for a third-person camera. The north event board remains visible beyond the two rooms. The main arrival-to-pit-to-events route should not pass through either room.
Main shot: player-height view from the concourse near the blue cat with black fedora, looking diagonally across BOTH open portals; show purposeful warm interiors and restrained category accents with enough depth to understand these are rooms. The pit occupies open space at right; a few benches remain on its rim. Do not divide the main room into cramped hallways. Make this version more intimate and lived-in: repaired tile, salvaged backstage dressing lights, folded cloth on a shelf, a restrained patchwork bulletin board. It should feel like the competitors' clubhouse inside a larger subway station, with very clear access. No more than three distant cat players, no humans.
Bottom vignettes: 'APPEARANCE ROOM' shows two distinct usable Locker and Prize stations; 'CAREER ROOM' shows separate Profile desk and Progression wall. Main title exact 'B / TWO CLUBROOMS'.

name: 03_pit_pavilion
title: C / PIT PAVILION
detail:
Primary proposal: group the four services into ONE compact freestanding horseshoe-shaped or oval SERVICE PAVILION on the WEST OUTER EDGE of the central pit. This is an island on the flat concourse, NOT against the perimeter wall and NOT sitting in the pit. Keep the pit floor empty for social gathering, and leave a broad walking passage on ALL sides of the pavilion so the route around it makes sense. The island consists of four clearly differentiated faces/bays, each about 3.5 metres wide: 'LOCKER' as an open wardrobe pod with a hat rail; 'PROFILE' as a low identity console; 'PROGRESSION' as a horizontal milestone panel; 'PRIZE COUNTER' around the optional rear/outer face. A slender overhead open skeletal frame says 'PLAYER HUB'; no massive opaque roof. Low consoles and sparse vertical wardrobe fins preserve views to the main north event board. Show the pavilion offset to the LEFT of the main arrival-to-events sightline, not a central obstacle.
Main shot: actual player-height view from the south concourse, cat with black fedora in foreground; see the island silhouette, a visible clear gap between it and the round pit, and a visible gap on its wall side. The pit and event board remain the right/central landmarks; the west wall behind the island has murals and occasional benches, so it is visually unmistakable that all services have been brought off the wall. One or two distant visitors make the gathering scale clear. Fit the island into the existing spacious station; no giant modern mall or rooftop scene. Use common rugged steel framing, worn enamel infill, warm downlights and restrained magenta-white address signage.
Bottom vignettes: an eye-level opposite-side view reveals 'PRIZE COUNTER' and 'PROGRESSION'; a closer scene detail illustrates the broad clear passage around the pavilion, caption 'CLEAR SOCIAL LOOP'. Main title exact 'C / PIT PAVILION'.
